text:
maria: heads-up — nightly GHA eval reporter spiked with a bunch of flaky 'upload artifact' failures overnight, looks time-window related.
kevin: saw that in the logs too, lots of 413s around 03:00 UTC from the uploader.
zoe: could be the new aggregation window in the reporter — we changed batch_window -> 60s in the quant-smoke tweaks last week.
maria: exact. PR 462 toggled window to 60s. @kevin can you paste the failing curl fragment?
kevin: ```
POST /upload/artifact 413 Payload Too Large
Trace: upload_size=5.2MB window_ms=60000 reporter_batch=25
```
samir: 5.2MB per shard is on the high side — our uploader should gzip; are we double-encoding anywhere?
maria: turns out the Buildkite -> GHA handoff uses an env var that already contains gzipped bytes and the GH action re-encodes, producing larger payloads.
zoe: also FYI actions/upload-artifact has backend throttling when many uploads hit at once, even if each is <10MB. concurrent bursts in a fixed 60s window can push us into errors.
maria: proposal: replace fixed 60s window with jittered uploads (30–90s) + exponential backoff on 413s. That should smooth bursts.
kevin: I'll prototype a tiny action wrapper that staggers uploads. quick sketch: ```yaml
- name: eval artifact upload (stagger)
  run: |
    python tools/upload_stagger.py --window-min 30 --window-max 90
```
and python pseudo: ```python
# upload_stagger.py (concept)
collect shards
group by test_id
sleep random(window_min, window_max)
for grp in groups:
  try:
    upload(grp)
  except HTTPError as e:
    if e.status == 413:
      retry with exp backoff
```
zoe: nice. If we do that we should also emit an "artifact_wait_ms" metric so we can correlate p95 spikes to upload contention.
eval-bot: nightly-eval-runner-42 failed 03:04 UTC — artifact-upload returned 413 (7 occurrences)
zoe: another observation: p50 latency for evals is stable, but p95/p99 for runner startup and eval completion jumped right when these upload failures started. could be tail latency from upload contention delaying job finalization.
maria: agreed — upload contention can delay step finalization which then inflates p95 for the whole eval. we saw this after we added quantize-smoke which increases artifact count per job.
samir: short-term for PR gating: add a tiny smoke job that runs quantized model but disables artifact uploads (or uses a dry-run flag). that will keep gating sensitive to model regressions without being polluted by artifact churn.
kevin: plan: open an RFC branch with three changes — 1) GHA staggered upload action, 2) Buildkite helper script to chunk+gzip shards, 3) dashboard panels + metric tag for artifact_wait_ms and upload_attempts. i'll do prototype today and flip on staging nightly only.
zoe: +1, also add traces with tag upload_attempts so we can filter traces with >1 retry.
maria: created tickets: ENG-ML-912 (gha upload jitter), ENG-ML-913 (bk uploader helper), ENG-ML-914 (dashboard: artifact_wait_ms). linking in the RFC.
kevin: opening PR now, will ping for review. prototype logs look promising (fewer 413s in local runs).
samir: i'll update the PR gating docs and the eval-runner README to recommend smaller artifact chunks and the jitter approach :thumbsup:
kevin: ping me if you want to pair when I draft the action wrapper.
maria: thanks all — if this smooths uploads we can re-evaluate the p95/regression alerts and reduce noisy failures in CI.
kevin: noted, will run staged rollout to nightly for 48h then roll to PR gates if green.
zoe: added a short dashboard tile to track artifact_wait_ms and a filter for staging vs prod evals.
eval-bot: nightly-eval-runner-42 resolved after retry/backoff 03:40 UTC — no new 413s observed in last run.
maria: great signal, will monitor tomorrow morning.
